narrative.overview:
The memo is produced by a tool, and the tool looks like one: the same language as Kai's Lotwise massing app, which is the pinned precedent. One sans, IBM Plex Sans at 13px, does nearly all the talking; IBM Plex Mono is reserved for what a machine wrote down, stamps, rule ids, hashes, paths and the lines to paste into a shell. Slate ink on a cool grey page, with white panels separated by a 1px line and a whisper of shadow. Corners are small, 4 to 6px, and buttons are dark ink that lifts on hover and sinks on press. Nothing is decorative; the page is dense the way a good drawing set is dense, and it stays calm because every element has a fixed job.

Colour is meaning. Blue is for links, focus, the selection and the step you are on; amber is for what is pending, the "not sure" answer, the engine still loading, a benchmark line; green, yellow, red, blue and grey mark the six statuses, always beside the printed word, never instead of it. The status strip under the step bar carries one line of feedback for every action, with a dot that says info, busy, ok or error. The massing drawings sit on white paper in both themes and keep Lotwise's drawing tones: envelope blue for the proposed mass, lane grey for the outright one, a red dashed line for the setback envelope, amber dashes for the staff benchmark.

Two things it is not, confirmed: not a dashboard (no gauges, KPI tiles, charts for their own sake, no icon-and-heading cards as page structure) and not a startup landing page (no gradients, glass, hero numbers, floating shadows or marketing voice).

The home page in front of the tool speaks the same language at the same density, and borrows the drawing set's own devices where it needs structure: a week ruler on a sheet with a title block, a schedule with numbered general notes, and a sheet issued for review to close on. When something changes between two readings of the rules, it is marked the way a drawing marks a revision.
keyCharacteristics: One sans at 13px with 11px uppercase keys; mono only for machine-written text.
Slate ink, cool grey page, white panels; dark mode is the same tool at night, not an inversion.
Buttons are ink-filled; the secondary ones take the group grey. Hover lifts, press sinks 1px.
A status is a word on a tinted pill with a round mark and a glyph before it.
Numbered badges stand in for section numbers; step panels and answer cards share them.
Drawings are always on white paper, whatever the theme.
A comparison is a revision: a delta with its letter beside whatever changed.

rules.name: The Marked Word Rule
rules.body: A status is a printed word with a coloured mark before it. The colour never appears without the word, and the word never appears without its mark.

rules.name: The Pending Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means not yet settled: a loading engine, an unsaved edit, an unsure answer, an uncertain finding, a benchmark still under negotiation. It is never a highlight, and never text on white: amber itself is 3.3:1, so words take Uncertain Text and fills take Amber Ink.

rules.name: The White Paper Rule
rules.body: Drawings and the Revit sheet sit on white in both themes, with their own fixed inks; the theme changes the desk, not the paper. A light-token reset on paper re-declares the derived tokens too (the status marks are resolved where they are defined, so they would keep the night colours otherwise).

rules.name: The Revision Rule
rules.body: When two readings of the rules are compared, what changed carries a delta with its letter (A) and the comparison's answer sits right under the title block, before the three answers. Nothing else uses the delta.

rules.name: The Lead Sentence Rule
rules.body: In any finding, the first sentence is Ink and the continuation is Muted. Hierarchy inside a paragraph comes from colour, not weight.

rules.name: The Key Rule
rules.body: Every small uppercase label is the same key: 11px, 600, 0.06em. It names a group, a column, a figure or a title-block field, and nothing else. It never sits above a heading as a kicker: a heading speaks for itself.

rules.name: The Machine Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono is for text a machine produced or will consume: stamps, ids, hashes, paths, shell lines, the as-of date. Human sentences are never set in mono.

rules.name: The One Pixel Rule
rules.body: A panel's shadow is one pixel; it says "sheet on a desk", not "floating". Only something that is actually above the page casts more.

dos: Do set everything in IBM Plex Sans at 13px with 11px uppercase keys, and keep mono for what a machine wrote.
Do print every status as a word with its round mark in front, on its wash.
Do fill buttons with Ink (secondary with Group), lift them on hover and sink them 1px on press.
Do keep Blue for links, focus and the active step, and Amber for what is pending.
Do keep panels at 6px radius, 12px by 14px padding, 1px Line and the one-pixel shadow, 12px apart.
Do keep the drawings on white paper in both themes with Lotwise's drawing tones.
Do mark a comparison as a drawing revision: a delta A beside each change, the answer under the title block.
Do reach for the drawing set's own devices (title block, schedule, general notes, an issued sheet) before a generic card.
donts: Don't build a dashboard: no gauges, KPI tiles, sparklines, or icon-plus-heading cards as structure.
Don't reach for a landing page's kit: no gradients, glass, hero numbers, floating shadows, marketing voice.
Don't bring back a serif, a 16px body, or large display type; the memo reads at drafting density.
Don't put a status colour on a button, a heading or a background that carries no status.
Don't add a toast, a second accent, or a shadow deeper than one pixel on anything at rest.
Don't use "N/A", a colour without its word, or a checkbox where "not sure" is a legitimate answer.
Don't set amber as text on white, put a key above a heading as a kicker, or end a page on a dark band of buttons.
